sentences.text: "That's Kowalski on the hull," he said, "the man who taught me to boil coffee over an engine block." Safety briefing at 0600: nobody walks within three meters of moving tracks, no exceptions, not even the director. Turret markings, bogie wheels, a crooked antenna — he named every part of the machine in that photograph like an old friend. Someone chalked the actor's mark directly onto the hull, and continuity made them photograph it before wiping. By noon the column had rolled through the village set four times, and the cobblestones were starting to crack. He'd been a gunner, he told us, and the periscope's narrow world was all he saw of France. "Cut — the second Sherman drifted out of frame again," the first AD barked into her radio. My sister kept the tape recorder running under a dish towel so his stories wouldn't vanish like the men in the pictures. Video village erupted when the drone shot caught all five vehicles cresting the ridge in perfect echelon. You could hear the loader's routine in his cadence — shell, breech, ready — even sixty years after his last fight. A camera car kept pace with the rolling column, its stabilized arm floating over the lead vehicle's turret. The memoir's third chapter, read aloud between bites of pie, described repairing a thrown track in freezing mud while shells walked the treeline. Cracked at the spine, the album fell open to the page where his memoir began, the ink faded but the handwriting steady. When Grandma refilled his cup, he pointed to a smudged photograph and whispered that the driver's seat still smelled of diesel in his dreams. Forty years of silence, and now the whole story spilling out over cold coffee. Each armored prop carries a fire extinguisher bolted inside the hull, hidden from every camera angle. Every November the ritual repeats: the album comes down from the shelf, the kitchen goes quiet, and the war returns in his careful voice. Rain had streaked the fake mud on the hull, so the art department mixed another batch of fuller's earth. Stunt rehearsal ran long: six hatch exits before anyone was allowed to touch the ignition. Nobody touched the pie while he described the night his platoon crossed the Roer under artillery. What is the meaning of the word tank?
